answer_1.quote: We train a sequence-to-sequence generative model CT-GAT (Cross-Task Gerative Adversarial ATtack) using adversarial sample data obtained from multiple tasks. To effectively learn the distributional characteristics from original sentences to adversarial sentences and generate diverse adversarial samples, we choose to utilize the encoder-decoder architecture of Transformer.
answer_1.outputs: Adversarial text samples (perturbed sentences) generated to attack victim classifiers

answer_2.quote: The perturbation degree is measured by the Levenshtein distance. Text quality is measured by the relative increase in perplexity (% PPL) and the absolute increase in the number of grammar errors (∆I). Semantic similarity is an evaluative metric quantifying the extent to which the meaning of the original sentence is preserved post‑perturbation, represented by the cosine similarity of Universal Sentence Encoder (USE) vectors. ASR and Query Count are also reported.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluations ... we ask 5 evaluators to assess the following aspects sequentially: (1) whether the adversarial sample conveys malicious intent (or contains sensitive information), and (2) the degree to which the intended meaning of the original sample and the adversarial sample aligns, measured on a scale of 0‑2.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators judge (1) presence of malicious intent and (2) meaning preservation using a 0‑2 rating scale.
